We need to audit StakingVault.sol. It's a simple contract with reentrancy bug: in unstake, it sends ether before updating state. So attacker can re-enter unstake to drain more than they have. Since stakeOf[msg.sender] is not cleared before call, attacker can call unstake recursively, each time sending same amount? Actually amount = stakeOf[msg.sender]; initially amount = their stake. In first call, they get amount, then after call, totalStaked -= amount; stakeOf[msg.sender] = 0. But during reentrancy, before state cleared, stakeOf still holds amount, so second call will also see amount = stakeOf[msg.sender] (still original amount) and send again. However after first external call returns, the state will be cleared, but the reentrant call occurs during the external call, before the clearing. So attacker can drain amount repeatedly until gas runs out. So they can drain all ether from contract, not just their stake. So victim loss: other users lose their stake.

We need to confirm if any guard prevents reentrancy: none. So exploit works.

We need to define victim_enter and victim_exit: victim deposits some ether, then later withdraws (unstake). In honest scenario, victim gets back their deposit. In attack scenario, attacker reentrancy drains contract before victim can withdraw, causing victim to get less.

But the victim's withdraw is after attack? The harness runs victim_enter, then attack, then victim_exit. So we can have victim deposit 1 ether, then attacker runs attack (unstake reentrancy) draining all ether, then victim attempts to unstake, but contract balance is zero, so they get zero.
